answers.value: The revised zonal capacity allocation: proposed per-zone capacity budgets (TIV/PML caps) across catastrophe peril zones, reallocated to keep modelled accumulations within internal PML appetite and treaty retention; scope = all peril zones in the reallocation proposal.
Allocation effective for the forward period (e.g. effective 2026-07-01 through the treaty year), based on the 2026-06 accumulation and cat model run.

The allocation proposal must show, per zone: current accumulation, proposed capacity budget, headroom created, PML impact and treaty-retention impact. A proposal missing PML/treaty impact for any zone is not put forward for sign-off.

Sum of proposed zonal capacities reconciles to the total portfolio capacity budget and net treaty retention; aggregate modelled PML under the new allocation recomputes within internal appetite (0 unreconciled zones).

The approved allocation and decision record are saved to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio-Exposure/Capacity-Allocation/2026-Q3/ with effective date, approver and version; the superseded allocation is retained 7 years.

Zones where the requested capacity exceeds appetite are logged in Archer GRC with disposition (approve with condition / reduce / require reinsurance); conditional approvals carry a documented condition and review date.

checklist.step: Set zonal capacity within concentration limits
checklist.value: The revised allocation assigns per-zone capacity so modelled accumulation stays within documented concentration limits.

testing.value: Under the approved allocation, every zone's projected accumulation is within its concentration limit; 0 zones over limit without a documented condition.

checklist.step: Support the decision with zonal reporting
checklist.value: The allocation decision is backed by zonal accumulation and PML reporting reconciled to in-force exposure.

testing.value: Allocation figures trace to the certified zonal roll-up and cat model run; sampled zones reconcile within 0.5%.

checklist.value: Capacity reallocation is approved by the role with the correct authority per the Underwriting Authority Matrix v3.2 (CUO for portfolio-level capacity).

testing.value: The recorded approver holds the required authority level; 0 allocations live without an in-authority sign-off.

answers.value: Post-event exposure assessment following a named storm, earthquake or wildfire: in-force TIV, policy count and modelled/estimated loss within the event footprint, plus reinsurance recovery position; scope = all policies intersecting the event geography.
From the event date through the assessment cutoff (e.g. event 2026-06-14, assessment as at 2026-06-21), refreshed as footprint data matures.

Each in-footprint record carries: policy key, geocode, TIV, coverage, modelled/estimated loss and treaty attachment. Records without a geocode or coverage detail are worked before the exposed-loss estimate is issued.

In-footprint TIV and policy counts reconcile to Guidewire PolicyCenter in-force; gross modelled loss plus expected reinsurance recovery equals net retained estimate, tying to the treaty terms in Sapiens ReinsurancePro (variance <=1%).

The post-event assessment and footprint exposure extract are saved to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio-Exposure/Post-Event/2026-Storm-Name/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years for reserving and reinsurance recovery.

Data gaps (ungeocoded exposure, coverage ambiguity) are logged in Archer GRC with disposition and clear-by date; material adverse deviation from the pre-event PML estimate escalates to the CUO, Chief Actuary and Head of Reinsurance.

Pre/post comparison: the pre-event modelled PML for the affected zone is compared to the post-event exposed-loss estimate; the delta and its drivers (footprint vs modelled, demand surge) are documented and reconciled.
The assessment is linked to the event/CAT response record and to the reinsurance recovery notification; cross-referenced to the claims event code in Guidewire and the Sapiens ReinsurancePro cession.
All in-force policies intersecting the event footprint (census), with a sample of high-TIV exposed locations validated against the hazard footprint and claims first-notice data.

PASS = exposed TIV reconciles to in-force, gross-to-net ties to treaty terms, and the estimate is within a defensible range of early claims signal; FAIL = unreconciled exposure or a net estimate inconsistent with treaty attachment.

Where the estimate diverges materially from early claims experience, the footprint and loss factors are re-run with Actuarial, the assessment re-issued, and the revision logged in Archer GRC with rationale.
Acceptance = post-event assessment reviewed by the CUO with Actuarial concurrence, exposed TIV reconciled, gross/net consistent with treaties, pre/post PML delta explained.
SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio-Exposure/Post-Event/2026-Storm-Name/ (assessment + footprint extract) and the Archer GRC post-event exception log.

checklist.step: Estimate exposed loss against PML basis
checklist.value: Post-event exposed loss is estimated using the cat model footprint and compared to the pre-event PML for the affected zone.

testing.value: The pre-event PML and post-event estimate are documented with a reconciled delta and drivers; 0 unexplained material variance.

checklist.step: Aggregate exposed TIV in the footprint
checklist.value: In-force TIV intersecting the event footprint is aggregated and reconciled to bound exposure.

testing.value: Exposed TIV reconciles to in-force within 1%; sampled locations validate against the hazard footprint.

checklist.step: Back-test model output against the actual event
checklist.value: Modelled loss is compared to developing claims experience to calibrate future cat guideline and capacity decisions.

testing.value: Modelled vs actual variance is recorded and fed to model validation; lessons logged for the next accumulation cycle.
